en.authority: Swiss Federal Department of Finance / official amending protocol
en.text:
Article 10 — Dividends

1. Dividends paid by a company which is a resident of a Contracting State to a resident of the other Contracting State may be taxed in that other State.

2. However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

3. Notwithstanding paragraph 2, the State of the company paying the dividends shall exempt the dividends if the beneficial owner is (a) a company, other than a partnership, resident in the other State which directly holds at least 10 per cent of the capital of the payer for an uninterrupted period of at least one year; (b) a qualifying pension fund or similar institution resident in the other State; or (c) the central bank of the other State.

en.authority: Swiss Federal law (Fedlex); English rendering for web display
en.text:
Article 11 — Interest

Interest arising in a Contracting State and beneficially owned by a resident of the other Contracting State is taxable only in that other State, subject to the permanent-establishment / fixed-base exception and the arm's-length limitation for excessive interest. This English wording is a non-authentic translation for web display; the official treaty text controls.

en.authority: Swiss Federal Department of Finance / official amending protocol
en.text:
Article 12 — Royalties

Under Article 12(2), royalties may in principle be taxed in the source State up to 10 per cent of the gross amount. The Protocol to the Convention provides that, for as long as Switzerland does not under its domestic law levy withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents, paragraph 2 does not apply and the tax charged in the Contracting State in which the royalties arise shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

en.authority: Swiss Federal Department of Finance / official amending protocol
en.text: Article 10(2) — general dividend branch. If the beneficial owner is a resident of the other Contracting State and the holding is not effectively connected with a permanent establishment in the source State, source-State tax shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

en.authority: Swiss Federal Department of Finance / official amending protocol
en.text: Article 10(3)(a) — company exemption branch. The source State shall exempt the dividends if the beneficial owner is a company other than a partnership, resident in the other State, which directly holds at least 10 per cent of the capital of the paying company for an uninterrupted period of at least one year; the holding must not be effectively connected with a permanent establishment in the source State. Czech source-State rate: 0 per cent.

en.authority: Swiss Federal Department of Finance / official amending protocol
en.text: Article 10(3)(b) — pension-fund exemption branch. The source State shall exempt the dividends if the beneficial owner is a qualifying pension fund or similar institution resident in the other Contracting State and the holding is not effectively connected with a permanent establishment in the source State. Czech source-State rate: 0 per cent.

en.authority: Swiss Federal Department of Finance / official amending protocol
en.text: Article 10(3)(c) — central-bank exemption branch. The source State shall exempt the dividends if the beneficial owner is the central bank of the other Contracting State and the holding is not effectively connected with a permanent establishment in the source State. Czech source-State rate: 0 per cent.

en.authority: Condition-aware summary of the original Article 10 treaty branch; official treaty text controls
en.text: Original Article 10(2)(a) — historical participation branch applicable through 31 December 2013. Source-State tax shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross dividend if the beneficial owner is a company other than a partnership that directly owns at least 25 per cent of the capital of the paying company and the holding is not effectively connected with a permanent establishment in the source State. The 2012 Protocol replaced this branch from 1 January 2014.

en.authority: Condition-aware summary of the approved Stage 6 treaty rule; official treaty text controls
en.text: Article 11 — Interest: the treaty's exclusive residence-state taxation applies where the recipient is a treaty resident and beneficial owner, the interest is not effectively connected with a permanent establishment or fixed base in the source State, and the amount satisfies the treaty arm's-length limitation.
